text: This clock runs slow.
Nobody touched it.
Its twin, outside, keeps perfect time.
Broken? Or is time slower in there?
Take it apart.
Lift a clock about a foot. It runs faster.
Measured, with two atomic clocks.
Stand a couple of steps higher, and you age faster.
Over seventy-nine years, that adds up to about ninety billionths of a second.
Gravity slows time.
Stronger gravity, slower clocks.
Longhour asks: what if you made the gravity?
A sealed cabin. A dense ring spins around it.
Spec: the cabin clock loses one second a day.
Trial one. Twenty-four hours. One second behind.
Trial two. Ring at full speed. One hour behind.
Trial three: a volunteer.
One day passes inside. Outside, a week.
One catch.
Inside, nothing feels slow.
Her watch, her pulse, her thoughts. All slow together.
She gets no extra time.
She just steps out into the future.
There is no way back.
Longhour is cleared.
As a one-way trip to the future.
Next case Sunday. Follow comp and grow.
